key_result: Low-dependence symmetric evaluators benefited from switching, but scalar dependence discounting without routing caused severe search starvation at high dependence. In the class-asymmetric regime, routing to a materially stronger B increased the information-per-call proxy but produced no reliable archive-quality or false-promotion improvement under any scalar/separate rule, indicating decision-rule mismatch rather than only evaluator-selection mismatch.
public_evidence: arXiv:2601.22336 shows class-dependent judge coupling generally requires quadratic Bayes log-odds, whereas class-independent coupling can use correlation-adjusted linear weights; this independently supports testing explicit joint/class-dependent aggregation next.
